ozet: His lineage; 'Abd al-Muttalib's vow and the hundred camels; the marriage of 'Abdullah and Amina; the death of 'Abdullah and the birth in the Year of the Elephant. The episode ends with the search for a wet nurse.

b03-s01: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was the son of 'Abdullah and the grandson of 'Abd al-Muttalib. His lineage goes back to Quraysh through Hashim, 'Abd Manaf and Qusayy.

Years later the Messenger of Allah would say: «Allah chose Kinana from the descendants of Ishmael; He chose Quraysh from Kinana; He chose the sons of Hashim from Quraysh; and He chose me from the sons of Hashim.»
b03-s02: The story begins with a vow. According to the reports, when 'Abd al-Muttalib met opposition from Quraysh while digging the well of Zamzam, he made a vow: if he were to have ten sons and they grew old enough to protect him, he would sacrifice one of them to Allah beside the Ka'ba.
When his sons numbered ten and were old enough to protect him, 'Abd al-Muttalib told them of his vow, and they accepted it.
b03-s03: Following the custom of the day, lots were drawn with arrows beside the idol Hubal inside the Ka'ba. According to the reports, the lot fell on 'Abdullah, the son his father loved most.

When 'Abd al-Muttalib led him away to be sacrificed, Quraysh rose from their gathering places, came and stopped him: if he did this, people would make a custom of bringing their sons to be sacrificed.
b03-s04: Quraysh advised him to consult a woman who was believed to have knowledge of the unseen. They first went to Medina; according to the reports, they found her in Khaybar.

The woman asked how many camels the blood money for a person was among them; they said ten camels. Lots would be drawn between 'Abdullah and ten camels, and each time the lot fell on 'Abdullah, the camels would be increased until their Lord was satisfied.
b03-s05: They returned to Mecca and began drawing lots. Each time the lot fell on 'Abdullah, and the camels were increased ten at a time.
When the camels reached a hundred, the lot fell on the camels. 'Abd al-Muttalib insisted on drawing three more times; all three times the lot fell on the camels.
A hundred camels were sacrificed, and 'Abdullah was saved.
b03-s06: From there 'Abd al-Muttalib took his son 'Abdullah by the hand to Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf, chief of the Banu Zuhra, and married him to his daughter Amina.
In lineage and standing, Amina was at that time the most distinguished woman of Quraysh.
b03-s07: As the Messenger of Allah related, his mother had seen a dream while she was pregnant. According to the reports, she had been told to name the child to be born Muhammad (in one report, Ahmad).
b03-s08: 'Abdullah went to Syria for trade. On the way back he fell ill in Yathrib, died among the Banu al-Najjar, his father's maternal uncles, and was buried there.
According to the preferred report, this happened while Amina was pregnant; the Prophet would come into the world without seeing his father.
b03-s09: The Qur'an refers to this orphanhood: «Did He not find you an orphan and protect (you)?»
b03-s10: The Prophet was born in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, 571 CE, on the twelfth of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal.

Years later, when the Messenger of Allah was asked about fasting on Mondays, he would say: «That is the day I was born, and the day I was sent as a prophet, or the day (revelation) was sent down to me.»
b03-s11: Amina sent word to 'Abd al-Muttalib: «A boy has been born to you; come and see him.»
'Abd al-Muttalib came. Amina told him what name she had been told to give the child. The child was named Muhammad.
b03-s12: According to the reports, 'Abd al-Muttalib took him and entered the Ka'ba; there he prayed to Allah and gave thanks for the blessing He had given.
Then he gave him back to his mother and began to look for a wet nurse for him.
